Welcome to St Crispin's Infant School
Starting school in September 2027?
Their first day starts here.
It might seem far away now, but parents only have until January 2027 to choose their preferred schools.
If your child is starting school in September 2027, we warmly invite you to our Early Years Open Evening on Thursday 24th September at 5pm.
Come along with your child and meet our staff, have a tour of our school, and see how St Crispin’s is going to be the perfect choice for your child!
To book a space, please use the link below:
Why choose St Crispin's?
St Crispin’s is a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child can lay the foundations for learning and life. We support our children and families to develop the tools to succeed at St Crispin’s and beyond.
Our School Values
We support our children and families to develop the tools to succeed at St Crispin’s and beyond. Our values are brought together under the acronym LEARN, reflecting our belief that every day is an opportunity to discover, develop, and shine!

SEND Interventions
Lego Therapy is a fun and engaging therapeutic approach that uses LEGO building activities to support social communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. Originally developed for children with autism, it has proven to be beneficial for individuals with a wide range of social and developmental challenges. In a typical session, children take on different roles—such as builder, supplier, and engineer—encouraging collaboration, turn-taking, and clear communication. This hands-on, play-based method not only enhances social interactions but also boosts confidence, creativity, and fine motor skills. By fostering a supportive and inclusive environment, Lego Therapy helps individuals develop essential life skills in an enjoyable and meaningful way.
Drawing and Talking Intervention is a gentle, child-centred therapeutic approach that helps children process emotions and experiences through creative expression. Designed to support emotional well-being, this intervention encourages children to draw freely while engaging in relaxed, non-directive conversations with a trusted adult. This safe and nurturing process allows them to explore their thoughts and feelings at their own pace, helping to build self-awareness, confidence, and emotional resilience. Particularly beneficial for children who struggle to express themselves verbally, Drawing and Talking provides a comforting outlet for processing difficult experiences, reducing anxiety, and improving overall mental well-being in a natural and supportive way.
Dynamo Maths is a specialised intervention programme designed to support children with dyscalculia and maths-related learning difficulties. Using a structured, research-based approach, it identifies gaps in foundational math skills and provides personalised, multi-sensory activities to strengthen understanding. The programme combines engaging digital exercises with hands-on learning, making maths more accessible and enjoyable for learners who struggle with numbers. By building confidence, improving number sense, and reinforcing essential math concepts, Dynamo Maths empowers children to develop a positive relationship with mathematics, helping them to succeed in school and beyond.
Clicker 8 is an innovative literacy support tool designed to help children of all abilities develop their reading and writing skills. This user-friendly software offers a range of features, including word prediction, speech feedback, and customisable writing grids, making it especially beneficial for learners with dyslexia, speech and language difficulties, or other additional needs. By providing a supportive and engaging learning environment, Clicker 8 helps to boost confidence, encourage independent writing, and enhance language development. Its multi-sensory approach ensures that students can express their ideas more easily, making literacy learning more accessible, enjoyable, and inclusive.
Precision Teaching is a highly effective, data-driven approach designed to improve academic and behavioural skills through consistent practice and measurement. This method focuses on tracking a learner’s progress with precision. By breaking down skills into smaller, manageable tasks and providing frequent, targeted practice, Precision Teaching helps individuals gain mastery and build confidence in areas such as math, reading, and communication. The approach is personalised to each child’s pace, ensuring that progress is continuous and measurable. This fosters a sense of accomplishment, motivation, and long-term success in both educational and everyday settings.
Little Wandle Catch-Up Support is an excellent intervention program designed to help children who are struggling with early reading skills. Based on the evidence-backed Little Wandle Letters and Sounds phonics program, this catch-up support provides targeted, individualised lessons that focus on reinforcing key phonics and reading skills. The program offers a structured, systematic approach that builds children’s confidence in decoding and reading words, making learning both fun and effective. By offering additional practice in a supportive environment, Little Wandle Catch-Up Support helps children catch up with their peers, preventing gaps in learning and fostering a positive attitude toward reading and literacy. It ensures that every child can succeed, regardless of their starting point.
Language Through Colour is a visual and multi-sensory approach designed to support language development, particularly for children with speech and language difficulties. This method uses color-coded systems to help children understand and organise language concepts such as sentence structure, parts of speech, and grammar. By associating colours with specific language functions, children can more easily recognise and apply these concepts in both written and spoken communication. The visual nature of Language Through Colour makes it especially effective for learners with additional needs, such as those with dyslexia or autism, as it provides a clear, structured way to process complex language skills. This approach boosts confidence, enhances communication, and supports long-term language development in a fun and engaging way.
Fizzy is a fun, structured programme designed to support the development of social communication skills for children, particularly those with speech, language, and social interaction challenges. Through engaging activities and interactive exercises, Fizzy helps children understand and practice key social skills such as taking turns, listening, making eye contact, and interpreting body language. The programme focuses on building confidence in social situations, fostering positive relationships, and improving overall communication abilities. By providing a safe and supportive environment for practicing social skills, Fizzy not only enhances children’s ability to connect with others but also contributes to their emotional well-being and success in everyday interactions.
BEAM Balance, Education, and Movement is an exciting and dynamic program that combines physical activity with learning to support children’s development. The programme integrates movement and mindfulness with academic content, helping children improve their focus, coordination, and emotional regulation while reinforcing important educational concepts. Through fun, engaging activities such as balance exercises, stretching, and interactive games, BEAM encourages physical activity that enhances brain function, boosts concentration, and reduces stress. By promoting physical well-being alongside cognitive skills, BEAM supports children in developing a balanced, healthy lifestyle and helps them feel more confident and ready to learn. This holistic approach not only improves learning outcomes but also fosters emotional resilience and overall mental health.
Speech Link Intervention is a targeted, evidence-based program designed to support children with speech, language, and communication difficulties. It provides structured, personalised activities that address a range of speech and language challenges, from articulation and fluency to vocabulary development and sentence structure. Through interactive, fun exercises and activities, Speech Link helps children improve their ability to express themselves clearly and confidently. The programme is tailored to meet individual needs, ensuring progress at each child’s own pace. By improving communication skills, Speech Link fosters greater social interaction, academic success, and emotional well-being, empowering children to fully participate in their learning and everyday life.
Language Link Intervention is a comprehensive program designed to support children with speech, language, and communication needs, helping them develop essential language skills for academic and social success. The programme offers tailored activities that target specific areas of language development, such as vocabulary, sentence structure, comprehension, and verbal reasoning. By providing a structured yet flexible approach, Language Link ensures that children can progress at their own pace, building confidence in their communication abilities. The intervention is beneficial not only for children with language delays but also for those who may struggle to keep up with peers in classroom settings. Through engaging activities and clear, consistent support, Language Link empowers children to improve their language skills, boosting their academic performance, social interactions, and overall well-being.
Clever Hands Intervention is a hands-on program designed to support children in developing essential fine motor skills through engaging and purposeful activities. It focuses on improving hand-eye coordination, finger strength, dexterity, and control, which are crucial for tasks such as writing, drawing, using scissors, and self-care activities. By incorporating a variety of fun, tactile tasks like threading, building, and manipulating objects, Clever Hands helps children build the motor skills needed for everyday life and academic tasks. The programme not only enhances physical abilities but also boosts confidence, independence, and concentration. As children gain mastery over these skills, they are better equipped to succeed in school and feel more confident in their abilities.
Sensory Circuits Intervention is a dynamic and structured program designed to support children by providing sensory input that helps regulate their emotions, focus, and physical energy. The program consists of a series of activities tailored to stimulate different senses, such as balance, touch, and movement, in a structured sequence. These activities include tasks like jumping, balancing, and stretching, which help children calm, energise, or focus, depending on their individual needs. Sensory Circuits is especially beneficial for children who struggle with sensory processing difficulties, anxiety, or attention challenges, as it helps them better manage their emotions and behaviour. By promoting self-regulation and improving concentration, Sensory Circuits empowers children to feel more settled, engaged, and ready to learn, contributing to their overall well-being and success in both school and daily life.

We are committed to delivering a fully inclusive environment by providing equitable opportunities for all. Our approach is underpinned by our core values of collaboration, inclusion, ambition, innovation and nurture.
We believe that all children have the right to succeed and we aim to meet the individual needs of our pupils at all times. There will be no barriers to achievement within our learning community and our teachers will build strong relationships to facilitate the learning of all. We hold the same expectations for pupils with special educational needs and/ or disabilities (SEND) as for those without but remain fully aware that some children require a different approach in order to achieve success.
For full, detailed information about our support for children with SEND please view our SEN Policy and SEN Information Report on our policies page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Curriculum - St. Crispin's Infant School
pageCache.text:
At St. Crispin’s Infant School, we believe we are laying the foundations for learning and life by providing a curriculum that is purposeful and relevant. It is designed around our belief that each child is unique and can achieve their full potential as lifelong learners. The progressive structure of lessons allows children to explore, embed and develop expertise.
You can find out more about our curriculum in the tabs below.
Key Stage 1 Curriculum Cycle B 2025-26
Key Stage 1 Curriculum Cycle A 2024-25
Our children follow a broad and balanced curriculum, underpinned by the latest EYFS Framework Nov 2024. There are seven areas of learning and development. All areas of learning and development are important and inter-connected. EYFS Practitioners consider the individual needs, interests and stage of development of each child in their care in order to plan a challenging and enjoyable experience for each child in all of the areas of learning and development. Three areas are particularly crucial for igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning and for building their capacity to learn, form relationships and thrive. These are known as the three Prime areas of learning.
At the Stour Academy Trust, our priority is both the teaching of reading skills and the enjoyment of literature, enabling children to become lifelong, confident readers. We have a strong focus on speech and language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
We believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers regardless of their background, needs, abilities and age, and are determined to make this happen. Our aim is that by the end of year 6, pupils’ reading and writing is sufficiently fluent and effortless for them to manage the general demands of the curriculum in year 7, across all subjects and not just in English.
This is why we teach reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Nursery/Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school. Comprehension skills develop through pupils’ experience of high-quality discussion with the teacher, clear teacher modelling of effective reading strategies, as well as from reading and discussing a range of stories, poems and non-fiction
We value reading as a crucial life skill. By the time children leave us we want them to read confidently for meaning and regularly enjoy reading for pleasure. Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success.
We ensure that there is a balance of teaching instruction and instilling a love of reading. At the forefront of our reading curriculum is our ‘reading for pleasure’ agenda, where we strive to provide experiences that encourage children to be intrinsically motivated to read, through ensuring they experience the rewards that reading practices bring. All pupils must be encouraged to read widely across both fiction and non-fiction to develop their knowledge of themselves and the world in which they live, to establish an appreciation and love of reading, and to gain knowledge across the curriculum. Reading widely and often increases pupils’ vocabulary because they encounter words they would rarely hear or use in everyday speech. Reading also feeds pupils’ imagination and opens up a treasure-house of wonder and joy for curious young minds (2014 National Curriculum).
We have developed a programme of reading aloud to all pupils from Reception to year 6. We read aloud to children every day and across the school day as a part of the timetabled 5 a day reading diet. Through reading aloud teachers develop children’s key listening skills and model active thinking aloud skills and teach children to be text tellers and storytellers. This enables them to ‘talk like a book’ and notice more about text. Active listeners are likely to turn into active readers who build meaning. Teachers choose these books carefully as we want children to experience a wide range of books and genres, including books that reflect the children at the Stour Academy Trust and our local community as well as books that open windows into other worlds and cultures. In reading lessons and when reading at home, children from Reception to year 6 have access to Apps that encourage children to read for pleasure and to increase their reading mileage.
Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Resources for Parents
To find out more about Reading in the Primary English curriculum click the link below
Primary English Curriculum
It is our intent to facilitate our pupils’ development as effective communicators who can confidently use both spoken and written English.
Our goal is for our children to develop into enthusiastic, fluent, and responsive readers, writers, and orators who can learn and gain pleasure from the written word. Our high-quality Literacy curriculum, which develops reading comprehension and writing composition, fosters a whole school love of reading and writing. By placing quality children’s literature at the heart of Literacy learning, we aim to inspire creativity and critical thinking.
We incorporate the Centre for Literacy in Primary Education’s Power of Reading approach into our curriculum. This approach emphasises the use of high-quality texts to engage pupils, stimulate their imaginations, and develop their writing skills. Through the Power of Reading, we provide opportunities for pupils to explore diverse literature, enhancing their understanding of different genres and styles while fostering a love of storytelling.
We strive to equip pupils with firm foundations in English, enabling them to succeed in education, employment, and to participate fully in society.
We embrace a variety of technologies to develop English learning and to allow all children, regardless of barriers, to access and successfully achieve their full potential.
We recognise that each child is an individual and has their own learning needs; therefore, we measure progress in line with stage rather than age, ensuring that every child can celebrate success.

Our science curriculum is varied, progressive, and encourages children to develop a sense of wonder and curiosity about the world around them. We intend for our children to gain and develop the essential enquiry skills and Scientific knowledge necessary to become confident scientists; finding out why things happen the way they do.

In geography, we have designed our lessons around the 4 key areas of Geography focussing on locational knowledge, place knowledge, human and physical features and geographical skills. Our lessons intend to build on investigative and questioning skills throughout encouraging children to use secondary resources to find answers and extend their learning. The lessons are intended to improve children’s geographical vocabulary, map skills and geographical facts. We provide opportunities for consolidation and variety to ensure interest and progression in the subject.
You can find out more about the Geography curriculum below:
National curriculum in England: geography programmes of study – GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)
In history, our sequence of lessons are topic linked and investigative. The children are encouraged to look at artefacts and identify history facts and questions through looking at a broad variety of resources.
You can find out more about the History curriculum below:

DT at St Crispin’s is inspiring, rigorous and practical. Design and Technology encourages children to learn to think creatively to solve problems both as individuals and as part of a team. We encourage children to use their creativity and imagination, to design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values.
You can find out more about the Design and Technology curriculum below:

In Art we ensure all pupils produce creative, imaginative work through a sequence of lessons offering skills and knowledge progression. Learning within art enables all pupils to communicate what they see, feel and think through the use of colour, texture, form and pattern. Pupils become confident and proficient in a variety of techniques including drawing, painting, sculpting, and craft skills, e.g., collage, printing, weaving and patterns.

At St Crispin’s Infant School, we want all students to be able to thrive as responsible, digital citizens. Technology is everywhere and will play a pivotal part in our students’ lives. Therefore, we want to model and educate our pupils on how to use technology positively and safely. In computing pupils learning focuses on three strands i.e., computer science, information technology and digital literacy, throughout which we encourage our pupils to develop their ‘computational thinking’ and creativity to understand the importance and place for computing in the world in which we all live.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why choose St Crispin's? - St. Crispin's Infant School
pageCache.text:
Why choose St Crispin's Infant School?
Our School Values
At St Crispin’s, our values of Leadership, Equity, Ambition, Respect, and Nurture shape everything we do.
These values have been carefully chosen to support our children as they grow, explore, and thrive during their infant school years. Our goal continues – to ensure that St Crispin’s is a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child can lay the foundations for learning and life. We support our children and families to develop the tools to succeed at St Crispin’s and beyond.
We encourage even our youngest learners to show leadership by making positive choices, being role models to one another, and having the confidence to try new things.
Every child is valued, included, and supported. Equity means recognising the unique needs of each child and ensuring they have what they need to succeed.
We aim high for all pupils. Ambition inspires children to believe in themselves, persevere, and celebrate their achievements – both big and small.
Respect is at the heart of our school. We learn to care for ourselves, for each other, and for our environment.
A nurturing environment helps children feel safe, happy, and confident. We work closely with families to support children’s wellbeing and development.
An engaging Curriculum
Our thematic creative curriculum challenges our children to be well informed, critical and creative. Enriched through powerful experiences, children are inspired to produce their own personal and meaningful responses so their learning stays with them for the rest of their lives.
Our thematic creative curriculum prepares our children for the future by providing them with a well-rounded education that incorporates a variety of teaching methods and learning experiences that are engaging and meaningful to children.
These experiences can take many forms, including hands-on activities, school trips, learning projects, and visitors to the school, all of which can provide children with the insights, knowledge, and hands-on experiences that are related to the subject matter they are studying.
Learning through themed topics and experiences helps to make learning more interesting and relevant to our children, and can foster their curiosity and enthusiasm for learning, which ultimately can deepen their understanding and help them to retain information over the long term.
A modern and inclusive approach to teaching and learning
Most other schools teach children by direct instruction – where the teacher stands in front of a classroom, presents information and then gives the children a task to complete.
We believe that in order to provide our children with an education fit for the 21st century, teaching by direct instruction should only form a part of our children’s learning experience.
Instead, our teachers focus on teaching using more flexible, interactive and personalised methods that enable children to become more involved in the learning process and develop the collaboration, communication and creativity skills that our children will require to thrive in our modern society.
It’s important to understand the difference between passive and interactive teaching methods.
Passive teaching is a way of teaching where the teacher presents information to children that requires little to no active participation from the class. This method is good for teaching basic skills and knowledge, but it’s not always the best way to teach, because it doesn’t always help students think for themselves or solve problems.
In contrast, interactive teaching is designed to engage children and encourage them to participate in their own learning. These methods often involve hands-on activities, group work, and problem-solving tasks that require children to think critically and independently.
To prepare our children for the challenges of the 21st century, we promote the use of interactive teaching to help our children develop the skills they need to succeed in a rapidly changing world.
A child-centred, collaborative environment
In traditional classrooms, children are sat at front-facing desks and for the most part, do not move from that space all day.
In our child-centred classrooms, children are able to take advantage of our flexible classroom furniture to move around the class to suit the current learning activity. This gives children more opportunities to work with others, be social or work independently.
In our child-centred classrooms, the emphasis is on child-led learning and the development of critical thinking skills rather than learning through direct instruction and memorisation. Our teachers facilitate and support learning instead of transmitting information directly to the children and expecting them to learn from it.
In addition to traditional desks and chairs, in our child-centred classrooms, we use flexible seating to enhance the learning experience by allowing children to choose the seating arrangement that works best for them. This means the classroom environment can support different learning styles and needs.
For example, some children may prefer to sit on a comfortable beanbag chair, while others may prefer to stand at a standing desk. By providing a range of seating options, our teachers can accommodate the individual preferences and needs of their children, which can help them to be more engaged and focused in the classroom.
A supportive and close knit community
We firmly believe in the importance of strong collaboration between our school and parents, as we understand the vital role that parents play in their child’s education. We are dedicated to fostering a supportive and close-knit community where parents feel welcome, involved, and valued.
We regularly invite parents to our school to celebrate their children’s achievements and witness their progress. Our regular parent events provide parents with the opportunity to witness the growth and development of their children’s skills, knowledge, and creativity. These events also serve as a platform for children to take pride in their accomplishments and share their learning experiences with their families.
Throughout the year, we organise various events that encourage parental attendance and participation. These events include:
Curriculum Workshops: Parents are invited to attend these informative evenings to learn more about the curriculum, teaching methods, and classroom expectations. This allows parents to better support their child’s learning journey at home.
Parents evenings: Meetings between parents and teachers foster open communication and provide an opportunity to discuss a child’s progress, strengths, and areas for improvement.
Special Assemblies: During these events, we celebrate our children’s achievements, showcase their talents, and recognise their hard work.
Family Workshops: We host interactive workshops for parents and children, designed to help families better understand various subjects and engage in fun, educational activities together.
Annual School Fairs and Festivals: Our school organises fairs and festivals throughout the year, providing an opportunity for families to come together, have fun, and strengthen the sense of community within the school.
By actively engaging parents in their child’s education, we promote a supportive and collaborative learning environment that benefits both children and families. We are committed to maintaining strong connections with parents and encouraging their involvement in the educational journey of their children.
A caring, supportive and responsive EYFS
Our Early Years environment is caring, supportive and responsive to children’s individual needs. We allow our children to play and explore with a particular focus on the outdoor environment.
Playing outside gives children first-hand contact with weather, seasons, and the natural world, and outdoor environments offer children freedom to explore, use their senses, and be physically active and curious.
Playing outside is important for children’s overall development, as it provides a wide range of physical, social, emotional, and cognitive benefits. Here are four reasons why using the outdoor environment is important in the early years:
Physical development: Playing outside helps children to develop their gross motor skills, such as running, jumping, and climbing, as well as their fine motor skills, such as grasping and manipulating small objects.
Social development: Exploring the outdoor environment gives children the opportunity to interact with their peers and develop social skills, such as cooperation, communication, and conflict resolution.
Emotional development: Being outside can help children to feel calm, happy, and connected to nature, which can improve their emotional well-being.
Cognitive development: Outdoor play can also support children’s cognitive development, as it provides opportunities for exploration, discovery, and problem-solving.
An Inclusive School
We are committed to provide equal educational opportunities to all children, regardless of their abilities, backgrounds, or experiences.
Our classrooms are inclusive and recognise and value the diversity of children and create a learning environment where all pupils feel supported, valued, and challenged.
We use a variety of teaching methods and materials that cater to the diverse learning needs of children. This can include using visual aids, hands-on activities, and technology to help students understand and engage with the material.
By fostering a positive, supportive, and inclusive learning environment, inclusive classrooms help children develop the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in school and beyond.
We are committed to delivering a fully inclusive environment by providing equitable opportunities for all. Our approach is underpinned by our core values of collaboration, inclusion, ambition, innovation and nurture.
We believe that all children have the right to succeed and we aim to meet the individual needs of our pupils at all times. There will be no barriers to achievement within our learning community and our teachers will build strong relationships to facilitate the learning of all. We hold the same expectations for pupils with special educational needs and/ or disabilities (SEND) as for those without but remain fully aware that some children require a different approach in order to achieve success.
For full, detailed information about our support for children with SEND please view our SEN Policy and SEN Information Report on our key information page.
We follow the Mainstream Core Standards. This Kent guidance outlines support for children with SEND.
Mainstream Core Standards
Mainstream Core Standards Guide For Parents
Further information about services and opportunities for children with SEND is outlined in the Kent Local Offer.
www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/special-educational-needs
Click here for the latest Kent SEND newsletter for families:-
Support and advice is also available from IASK.
A commitment to nurture and well-being
We prepare children to succeed in their personal and professional lives by nurturing both their thinking and social-emotional skills.
We define bullying as “deliberately hurtful behaviour that is repeated over a period of time.” Bullying can take many forms, but the three main types are physical, verbal and indirect.
We encourage parents to inform us immediately if they suspect their child is being bullied. The sooner we know, the sooner we can act to stop it! Please see our anti-bullying policy for further details, including early signs of distress.
Bullying will not be tolerated in our school. It is everyone’s responsibility to prevent it happening and our policy contains guidelines for all members of the school community.
Our school takes part in the National ‘Anti-bullying week’ each year.
Throughout the year, children are encouraged to report all incidents of bullying to an adult and are supported in developing strategies to combat it, including the use of discussion and role play. Children are also taught awareness of ‘Cyber bullying’ throughout the year and this form of bullying will be dealt with in the same robust manner as any other form of bullying.
Nurture is at the heart of the school where we offer short term, inclusive, focused interventions to help with SEBD needs.
Our nurture room is a calm and inviting base for the children. We provide an inclusive curriculum where we work on literacy including Language Through Colour, maths and phonics.
In literacy we use a focus books that appeal to the children which allows us to offer them a stimulating and colourful learning experience.
Within the Nurture room we also address other aspects of development using child focused, tailor made interventions such as fine motor skills, sensory needs and social and emotional support. All of which are led by the 6 Principles of nurture:
Where needs are identified, well-being interventions will be implemented following a discussion with parents/carers. These may take place in a separate area or may form part of provision within the classroom. All classrooms have a dedicated area where children may withdraw to when they are feeling less settled and need to be in a quieter area in order to focus on their learning tasks. We call it the ‘calm down’ area.
Our aim is to ensure that not only do all pupils feel happy, secure and valued but that they are also able to work in a calm, pleasant and purposeful environment without disruption.
A smooth transition to Reception
Do you want to help your child’s transition into their first year at school?
From November to July, we host stay and play sessions to help familiarise children of pre-school age with our school.
Our sessions start with a welcome from our reception teachers, followed by lots of wonderful activities and will finish with a story or song.
No need to book, just turn up!
Please contact us for more information.

Inclusive classroom resources
Every one of our classes has an Inclusion Trolley packed full of resources. Inclusion trolley resources help to make sure that all children have access to tools that help them to be ready to learn. These resources help children with self-regulation, focus and attention.
Our Inclusion Trolley resources include
Fidget Resources
Fidget tools, sometimes referred to as sensory tools or fidget toys, are designed to help with self-regulation. Fidgets come in a variety of formats and have been shown to help children focus, relax and maintain attention to instructions.
Weighted Resources
Weighted resources help to provide constant, even, deep pressure input, creating a reassuring feeling to children.
Ear Defenders
Easy access to the ear defenders will reduce anxiety that the child might experience about possible trigger events, and enable them to have control over their auditory/hearing environment; however it is important that children are exposed to challenging sounds in a way that enables them to learn how to cope
Other Resources
Sensory timers are great in any classroom, but can be very helpful for children with autism, ADHD, sensory focus, hyperactivity issues, or anyone who is just distracted or anxious about the ticking numbers in our other timers. Now and next boards help with understanding the organisation of tasks and the school day.

St Crispin's CP Infant School Admissions
To apply for a place at St Crispin’s CP Infant School, you must apply through Kent County Council admissions. Follow the link below to apply.
Please also see our Admissions Policy for further information.
Admissions Policy 2025-26
Admissions Policy 2026-27
Admissions Policy 2027-28
Taken from www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/schools/school-places/appeal-a-school-offer
If your child is due to start primary school in September 2026, you can appeal if you are refused a place at one of your preferred schools on National Offer Day (Thursday 16 April 2026).
You must submit your appeal before Monday 18 May 2026 for it to be considered by Monday 20 July 2026. Any appeals received after this time will be heard within 40 school days from the deadline, or where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
For late applications, appeals should be heard within 40 school days from the deadline for lodging appeals where possible, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
For any appeals being lodged read the full copy of our privacy notice outlining your rights in relation to your personal data.
Contact for appeals: clerk.trust@stouracademytrust.org.uk
Once you have received an offer of a place and have accepted it, you will be required to complete our School Admission Form. Please contact the school office for a School Admission Form.
By completing and signing the School Admission Form you are confirming that you have read, understood and accepted the pages and policies below:
Charging and Remissions Policy
Online and Social Networking Policy
As many of you are aware, the school will often have events where parents/carers are invited into the school and we are sure that you would like to take pictures or videos of these events. If you wish to take pictures or videos at such an event, there is a strong possibility that other children will also be included within the picture. We do have some families, within our school, who do not wish for their children’s images to be taken and published.
Whilst we all enjoy and treasure images of our families and friends, we must ensure we protect and safeguard all children and staff, including those who do not want their images stored or shared online.
Therefore, in order to keep all members of the community safe, we must all ‘Think Before We Post’ online. At school, we are happy for parents and carers to take photos and videos for personal use of their individual children, however, we request that these images are not distributed or put online. This is to protect all members of the community. We would advise parents and carer’s to turn off their mobile devices during any performances and refrain from taking photos, so that the children are not being distracted whilst performing. There will be always be an opportunity at the end of a performance for parents and carers to take an individual photo of their child.
If this is found to be abused or not adhered to we will have to consider the prohibition of the use of cameras and videos at these events. We hope you will support us in this.
